sections.content: If you are looking for affordable real estate deals with real upside, Huntington, West Virginia deserves a serious look. Sitting along the Ohio River at the state's western tip, Huntington is West Virginia's second-largest city with a population of around 46,000. It is home to Marshall University, a regional medical hub, and a slowly diversifying economy. For investors who know how to spot value, the city offers some of the lowest entry prices in the eastern United States paired with rental demand that keeps vacancy rates manageable. Whether you are brand new to the game or a seasoned wholesaler expanding your territory, this guide covers everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in Huntington WV. If you are just getting started, bookmark the [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide as a companion resource.
Huntington WV Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Huntington's real estate market is what industry veterans call a "cash flow market." Home prices are well below the national median, which means you can acquire properties without massive upfront capital. As of 2024, the median home price in Huntington sits around $95,000 to $115,000, compared to the U.S. median of roughly $412,000. That gap is enormous. Distressed properties — the kind wholesalers and flippers love — can be found for $20,000 to $60,000. Rent for a solid three-bedroom single-family home typically runs $700 to $1,000 per month, which produces strong gross rent multipliers for buy-and-hold investors. The city has struggled with economic headwinds tied to the decline of coal and manufacturing, and that history has created a large inventory of undervalued, aging housing stock. That is exactly the type of environment where investors with vision and capital can thrive.
"The best real estate deals are found where others are afraid to look. Markets with low prices and steady rental demand are often the most forgiving places to build a portfolio from scratch."
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Huntington

Not every block in Huntington offers the same opportunity. Knowing where to focus your energy matters a lot in this market. Here is a breakdown of the areas that consistently attract investor interest.
Westmoreland and Highlawn

Located on the west side of the city, Westmoreland and Highlawn are among the more stable working-class neighborhoods. You will find well-built older homes, primarily from the 1930s through 1960s, that rent reliably to local families and Marshall University staff. Average acquisition prices in these areas range from $55,000 to $95,000 for turnkey or light-rehab properties. These neighborhoods work well for landlords building a long-term portfolio.
Guyandotte

Guyandotte is one of Huntington's oldest neighborhoods, annexed into the city in 1909, and it is experiencing quiet revitalization. Historic homes here have character and are attracting a small but growing number of first-time buyers and young renters. Investors who buy and lightly renovate here can see after-repair values climb into the $110,000 to $145,000 range, which leaves solid profit margins when you acquire correctly.
Central City

Central City has higher vacancy and more distressed inventory, which makes it a hunting ground for wholesalers. Properties here can be acquired well below $40,000, and with the right buyer list, assignment fees of $5,000 to $12,000 are achievable. This area carries more risk for landlords but offers high-reward opportunities for investors who move deals quickly.
Near Marshall University

The area surrounding Marshall University on 3rd and 4th Avenues is a natural student rental market. Small multi-family properties and single-family homes converted to rooming houses can produce per-bedroom rental income that beats the broader market. Vacancy during the school year is very low. Look for duplexes and triplexes priced between $70,000 and $130,000 for the best cash-on-cash returns.

Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Huntington WV
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is highly active in the Huntington market precisely because of the volume of distressed and inherited properties. Many sellers are motivated by deferred maintenance costs, delinquent taxes, or probate situations. A typical wholesale deal in Huntington might involve acquiring a contract on a 3-bedroom home for $28,000, then assigning it to a cash buyer rehabber for $38,000, netting a $10,000 assignment fee with zero money out of pocket. If you are new to this strategy, the [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide is an excellent starting point. Finding off-market motivated sellers is the key skill — check out [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) for proven prospecting methods that work in markets like Huntington.
Fix and Flip

Flipping works in Huntington, but you need to be disciplined with your numbers. The relatively low ARVs mean there is less margin for error than in higher-priced markets. A successful flip here typically involves buying a distressed property for $25,000 to $45,000, spending $30,000 to $50,000 on renovation, and selling for $100,000 to $140,000 depending on the neighborhood. That leaves a gross profit of $15,000 to $45,000 before holding and selling costs. Smaller, cleaner flips consistently outperform ambitious over-renovations in this market.
Buy and Hold Rentals

For long-term wealth building, Huntington's rental market is compelling. With acquisition prices this low, it is entirely possible to achieve cash-on-cash returns of 12% to 18% on stabilized rental properties. Section 8 housing vouchers are widely used in the city, which can provide landlords with guaranteed monthly payments from the Cabell County housing authority. Multi-family properties — duplexes and small apartment buildings — are particularly attractive for investors who want to maximize income per acquisition.

sections.content: Huntington WV Real Estate Market Trends in 2024 and Beyond

Huntington is navigating a slow but real revitalization. The city has received federal Opportunity Zone designations in several areas, which creates tax incentive programs for long-term investors. The Robert C. Byrd Institute and investments in healthcare infrastructure at Cabell Huntington Hospital are bringing new jobs to the region. The state of West Virginia has also launched remote worker incentive programs that are slowly attracting new residents from higher-cost states. None of this means Huntington is turning into Nashville overnight — but for patient investors, the trajectory is positive. Property values have appreciated modestly, averaging 4% to 7% annually in stabilized neighborhoods over the last three years, which adds equity growth on top of cash flow.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Huntington
Huntington is a market where boots-on-the-ground relationships make a significant difference. If you are investing remotely, here is how to do it right.

items: Build a local team first: Find a reliable property manager, a licensed contractor familiar with older Appalachian housing stock, and a real estate attorney before you buy your first deal.

Visit before you commit: A single trip to walk neighborhoods in person will teach you more than hours of online research. Central City and Guyandotte look very different from each other despite similar price points.

Use data tools to pre-screen deals: Platforms like [AIWholesail](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/huntington-wv) aggregate distressed property data and deal leads specific to the Huntington market so you can identify opportunities before making contact.
Understand water and foundation issues: Many Huntington homes were built on hillsides or near the river. Structural and drainage issues are common. Always budget for a thorough inspection.
Verify title carefully: Probate complications and cloudy title situations are more common in West Virginia than in many states. Work with a local real estate attorney, not just a title company.
Factor in property taxes: Cabell County property taxes are relatively low, which helps your cash flow math significantly compared to markets in Ohio or Pennsylvania.

Analyze every deal rigorously: Use the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to stress-test your offers before submitting, and cross-reference with the [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) guide to sharpen your underwriting skills.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When driving for dollars or pulling lists in Huntington, focus on properties with delinquent taxes, code violations, or out-of-state ownership. The Cabell County Sheriff's office publishes delinquent tax lists annually — this is one of the best free lead sources in the market and most investors ignore it.

"Cash flow markets like Huntington reward preparation over speed. The investors who take time to understand local conditions and build local relationships consistently outperform those who simply chase the lowest price per square foot."
Is Huntington WV Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Huntington is not a market for investors chasing rapid appreciation or luxury flips. It is a market for disciplined, numbers-focused investors who want strong cash flow, low entry costs, and a relatively large inventory of distressed opportunities to work through. If your strategy revolves around building passive income through rentals, generating consistent wholesale fees, or executing small-to-medium flips, Huntington fits that profile very well. The risks are real — economic fragility, older housing stock, and the need for strong local partnerships. But for investors who do their homework, the reward-to-risk ratio compares favorably to markets with much higher price tags.
